story: Taking ML to production with Rust
text: Right now, NVidia is designing their GPGPUs to run C++ code. [LINK] [VIDEO] With Intel just releasing oneAPI (aka Data Parallel C++) last month, and Khronos pushing SYCL as alternative to CUDA C++. It took 30 years for C++ to reach this stage, and in some domains (like embedded) it is still fighting for relevance. That is something to keep in mind whenever to advocate Rust as replacement for Domain XYZ.

story: My mesh shaders talk at XDC 2022
text: > I really wish that everybody would finally admit that the "fixed function pipeline" is dead There is a great deal of space between 'fixed function pipeline' (which no one is using) and 'all compute all the time' (which pretty much no one is using for real-time graphics either). > GPUs don't yet have a well-defined memory model Nvidia has a memory model. (I have heard--from an nvidia employee--that amd plays a bit more fast and loose.) [VIDEO] > GPUs don't have the equivalent of an MMU--so they can't be partitioned or protected. etc. You do not need an MMU to partition or to protect. (Not to say that GPU security isn't a shitshow.) > The problem is that switching to a "compute" model and making that work well would commodify the GPU--and that's the last thing that AMD and NVIDIA want. [LINK] look at where nvidia's revenue is coming from, and tell me again that they're not already there.
